name: Deep Dish Discovery Tour
description: Hit Chicago's most iconic food spots in one epic day. From deep-dish pizza to Chicago-style hot dogs, this quest takes you through the flavors that define the city.

stops.hint: Head to River North for the original butter crust experience.
Just a short walk away — grab an Italian beef combo.
Walk south on Michigan Ave. Follow your nose to the Chicago Mix.
Underground food paradise on Clark St. Perfect for dessert.

name: Chicago Street Art Walk
description: Explore Chicago's vibrant street art scene from Pilsen's murals to Wicker Park's creative energy. Bring your camera!

stops.hint: Start at 18th & Ashland and walk east along 18th Street.
Beautiful historic building right in the heart of Pilsen.
Take the Blue Line north to Damen. Browse the shops along Milwaukee Ave.
Reward yourself with tacos at this Wicker Park institution.
End the night at this hidden cocktail bar — look for the mural on Damen Ave.

name: Lakefront Adventure
description: A full day along Chicago's stunning Lake Michigan shoreline. Parks, beaches, wildlife, and the best skyline views in the city.

stops.hint: Start at The Bean for the ultimate Chicago photo op.
Walk north to the river. Grab a coffee and stroll along the water.
Continue east to the pier. Ride the Ferris wheel for lakefront views.
Head north on the trail. Rent a bike for the best experience.
Keep going north to Montrose. Relax on the beach and enjoy the skyline.
stops.address: 4400 N Lake Shore Dr, Chicago, IL 60640

stops.hint: Cut west into Lincoln Park. The zoo is free and open year-round!

name: Architecture River Walk
description: Chicago is the birthplace of the skyscraper. Walk along the river and Loop to see iconic buildings from the 1890s to today — no boat ticket required.

stops.hint: Start here on Michigan Ave to get oriented with the city's architectural history.
Cross the Michigan Ave bridge. The white terra-cotta towers glow at night.
Right next door — look for fragments of famous buildings embedded in the walls.
The iconic 'corn cob' towers on State St. One of Chicago's most photographed buildings.
Head south on Wacker Dr. Step onto The Ledge for a 103-floor glass-bottom view.

name: Museum Campus Explorer
description: Three world-class museums on one lakefront campus. Dinosaurs, galaxies, and an aquarium all in a single day — only in Chicago.

stops.hint: Start with SUE, the largest T. rex ever found. Main hall, can't miss it.
stops.address: 1400 S DuSable Lake Shore Dr, Chicago, IL 60605

stops.hint: Walk east along the lakefront. Catch the beluga whale feeding if you can.
stops.address: 1200 S DuSable Lake Shore Dr, Chicago, IL 60605

stops.hint: Keep walking to the tip of the peninsula — best skyline photo spot in Chicago.
stops.address: 1300 S DuSable Lake Shore Dr, Chicago, IL 60605

stops.hint: Loop back past the home of the Chicago Bears. Check out the iconic colonnades.
Hidden beach just south of the planetarium. Perfect for a break.
stops.address: 1200 S Linn White Dr, Chicago, IL 60605

name: Chicago Blues & Jazz Trail
description: Chicago shaped modern blues and jazz. Follow the music from legendary South Side clubs to downtown jazz lounges.

stops.spot_name: Chess Records / Willie Dixon's Blues Heaven
stops.hint: 2120 S Michigan Ave — where Muddy Waters, Chuck Berry, and the Stones recorded.
Head north to Wabash Ave. Live blues every night from a living legend's club.
South Dearborn St. The oldest jazz club in the city, running since 1947.
Take the Red Line to Lawrence. Al Capone's favorite speakeasy — still swinging.
Lincoln Park. Two stages, live blues till 4am. The real deal.

name: Hidden Chicago
description: Go beyond the tourist trail. Secret gardens, underground pedways, speakeasy bars, and spots most visitors never find.

stops.hint: Enter from the Metra station at Millennium Park. 40 blocks of underground tunnels.
stops.address: Millennium Station, 151 E Randolph St, Chicago, IL 60601

stops.hint: Hidden in plain sight at the south end of Millennium Park. A secret prairie oasis.
Look for the unmarked door on Dearborn St — classic speakeasy vibes.
Take the Red Line north. An open-air museum of Victorian architecture and famous Chicagoans.
Lincoln Park neighborhood. Statues of the Tin Man, Scarecrow, and Dorothy — a nod to L. Frank Baum's time in Chicago.
